claims.text: The soup base for all curries, including the vegetable-only option, is made with chicken-bone and dried-fish (niboshi) dashi, so vegetable dishes share an animal-derived broth.
A vegetable-only medicinal-herb soup curry is offered as a standing menu choice (though it is not vegan due to the broth and honey).

name: アレ!!ル トレッフル (Allez!! Le Trèfle)

claims.text: The chef cooks flexibly around seasonal ingredients rather than a fixed menu, so vegetable-forward plates can sometimes be requested, and there are some vegetable items such as pickled vegetables and nuts.
Signature dorayaki are made from wheat-flour batter and toast is baked on-site, so wheat is handled throughout the kitchen; no gluten-free preparation or separation is documented.
Dango are typically served with mitarashi/sweet tare based on Japanese soy sauce, which usually contains wheat; the shop does not document wheat-free tare.
Drinks lean toward tea and coffee, including Yamato tea and non-alcoholic mocktails, giving plant-based visitors some beverage options to ask about.

The core dish is rice-based onigiri, and a simple salt onigiri (こだわりの塩) and kombu onigiri are on the filling list, so plain rice-ball options exist for diners avoiding meat or fish if ordered carefully.

name: アストラルレイコーヒー (Astral Ray Coffee)

claims.text: All coffee and food items are available for takeout, which can help a traveler with dietary restrictions stick to simple, naturally compatible drinks like black drip coffee.

name: オーセンティックテーブル タバーン (Authentic Table Tavern)

claims.text: Sources seasonal Yamato vegetables from Nara and offers charcoal-grilled vegetable dishes such as broccoli, so some plant-forward options exist on the menu.
Menu is heavily wheat-based (udon, nyumen/somen, soba, dango) prepared in a shared kitchen, so cross-contact with gluten is effectively unavoidable.
Mitarashi dango sauce and noodle tare are typically based on wheat-containing soy sauce; no wheat-free soy sauce is documented.
Noodle and porridge sets use bonito (fish) dashi broth, and the menu includes herring and chicken dishes, so plant-based sweets share a fish-stock kitchen.

name: BAKERY GEN（ベーカリー ゲン） (BAKERY GEN)

claims.text: Conventional bakery that blends multiple wheat flours for its breads; flour is used throughout, so cross-contamination is unavoidable and there is no gluten-free production.
Breads commonly use eggs, dairy, custard cream, and butter; no vegan line is advertised and shared equipment/surfaces would contact animal-derived ingredients.
